title: SMC Multi Time Frame Analysis Approach (Trend Direction)

multi_timeframe_overview_and_tf_selectio.llm_summary: Multi Time Frame (MTF) analysis is essential for high probability trading. The presenter provides a complete Time Frame Selection table for 6 trading styles: (1) Positional Trading — Major Trend: Monthly, HTF: Monthly, LTF: Weekly, Entry TF: Daily. (2) Swing Trading — Major: Weekly, HTF: Weekly, LTF: Daily, Entry: H4. (3) Short Term Trading — Major: Daily, HTF: Daily, LTF: H4, Entry: H1. (4) Intra-day Trading — Major: H4, HTF: H4, LTF: H1, Entry: M15 or less. (5) Day Trading — Major: H4, HTF: H4, LTF: M15, Entry: M5. (6) Scalping Trading — Major: H1, HTF: H1, LTF: M15, Entry: M3. Key rules: choose 2-3 timeframes as your combination, stick to that combination for minimum 2-3 months, backtest first. Difference: intra-day traders may hold 2-3 days; day traders and scalpers close same day. The presenter personally recommends aligning just 2 timeframes minimum — if you learn to align HTF and LTF properly, you can become a very profitable trader.
key_rules: 6 trading styles with specific TF combinations: Positional (Monthly), Swing (Weekly), Short Term (Daily), Intra-day (H4/H1), Day Trading (H4/M15), Scalping (H1/M15)
Each style has 4 TFs: Major Trend, HTF, LTF, Entry Confirmation TF
Choose 2-3 timeframes as your combination
Stick to chosen TF combination for minimum 2-3 months
Backtest the TF combination before live trading
Intra-day: may hold 2-3 days. Day trader/Scalper: close same day
Minimum 2 TF alignment = sufficient for profitable trading
Major Trend TF = overall direction; LTF = entry confirmation

bearish_mtf_alignment_workflow.llm_summary: When the major trend (e.g., H4) is bearish and the sell zone is far from the current inducement, multi-timeframe alignment is used. The complete bearish workflow: (1) Major trend is bearish (shown in red). (2) Market breaks structure (BOS) and creates inducement (IDM). (3) When major trend's first valid inducement gets a candle body close above it → expect retracement toward sell zone. (4) The minor trend (e.g., M15, shown in black) will be temporarily bullish (counter-trend) as market retraces up. (5) When market approaches/taps the sell zone, observe the minor trend structure. (6) Map the minor trend: identify its IDM, BOS, and when the minor trend makes a Change of Character (CHoCH) → the minor trend shifts from bullish to bearish. (7) CHoCH = synchronization point — HTF (bearish) and LTF (now bearish) are aligned. (8) After CHoCH: mark the major IDM on LTF → find buy/sell zones below the IDM → enter at the NEW sell zone created from the reaction. Critical rule: NEVER trade the original sell zone directly — always wait for CHoCH on LTF, then trade the NEW zone that forms from the reaction.
key_rules: Major trend bearish (H4) + minor trend temporarily bullish (M15) = normal during retracement
Candle body close above major trend's first valid IDM → expect retracement to sell zone
Do NOT take direct entry at the sell zone — wait for LTF reaction
When market taps sell zone → observe LTF for Change of Character (CHoCH)
CHoCH on LTF = synchronization point — HTF and LTF now aligned bearish
After CHoCH: mark LTF major IDM → find NEW sell zone below IDM
Entry at the NEW sell zone (from reaction) — NOT the original HTF sell zone
Key: structure alignment is the most important factor, not specific POI zones

bullish_mtf_alignment_workflow.llm_summary: The bullish MTF alignment is the mirror of bearish. When major structure (H4/Daily) is bullish but the minor trend (M15) is temporarily bearish during a retracement: (1) Major trend bullish with buy zones below IDM. (2) When major trend's candle body closes below IDM → expect retracement down to buy zone. (3) Minor trend (M15) will be temporarily bearish. (4) When market taps the buy zone → observe LTF for CHoCH from bearish to bullish. (5) After CHoCH: mark LTF major IDM → find NEW buy zone below IDM. (6) Entry at the new buy zone with trend direction. The presenter emphasizes: this lecture covers trend-direction trades only (HTF trend = LTF entry direction). Counter-trend trading will be covered in the next lecture (V21).
key_rules: Bullish = mirror of bearish workflow

Buy zones below IDM on major trend
Candle body close below IDM → retracement to buy zone expected
After LTF CHoCH → mark new IDM → new buy zone → entry
This lecture = trend-direction trades only

why_order_blocks_get_swept.llm_summary: Many traders ask: why do order blocks fail? The presenter explains with the 'Early Buyers Trap' mechanism: (1) When market reaches an order block, some retail traders enter immediately (early buyers). (2) These early buyers create liquidity (their stop losses) below the order block. (3) Market sweeps this liquidity (takes out early buyers' stops). (4) After sweeping, market then moves in the original direction. The solution: NEVER take direct entry at any order block. Instead, wait for the reaction from the order block → when LTF shows structure shift (CHoCH) → trade the NEW zone that forms from the reaction. The presenter says Richard Wyckoff's methodology explains why OBs get swept — Wyckoff schematics make it very easy to predict which OB will be swept and which won't (covered in upcoming lectures). When you command structure and align LTF, you don't need to fear OB sweeps — you simply use structure to plan entries after the sweep. Key insight: if you understand structure, you can trade at ANY zone (not just the first OB or extreme OB) by aligning LTF structure.

real_chart_mtf_example_usdcad.llm_summary: Complete USD/CAD demonstration using H4 (major trend) and M15 (minor trend). TRADE 1: (1) H4 bullish trend identified. (2) Swing's valid IDM marked. (3) Below IDM: IOF/OB zone and Order Block zone identified. (4) Market takes IDM and taps IOF/OB zone on H4. (5) Switch to M15: market shows counter-trend (bearish) structure. (6) Market sweeps early buyers' liquidity below IOF/OB. (7) On M15: valid IDM marked → candle body closes above IDM → BOS confirmed → then swing high broken = CHoCH confirmed. (8) CHoCH = H4 and M15 now aligned bullish. (9) Mark major IDM on M15 → find hidden order block (last sell candle that swept previous candle's liquidity + FVG above) below IDM. (10) Direct buy entry at hidden OB → SL below safe low (low from which market CHoCH'd) → 1:3 R:R hit. TRADE 2: (11) H4 caution: market closed below major IDM → expect potential drop. (12) H4 drops to extreme Order Block zone → OB gets swept. (13) Early buyers trapped again → liquidity swept. (14) Switch to M15: map structure → CHoCH confirmed after BOS and swing break. (15) Mark new major IDM on M15 → find hidden OB/IOF below IDM. (16) Buy entry at hidden OB → SL below safe low → market rallies aggressively → 1:6.9 R:R achieved. (17) Compare H4 and M15 side-by-side: even though H4 OB was swept, LTF structure alignment produced a beautiful entry with excellent R:R.
key_rules: USD/CAD H4 bullish + M15 alignment for 2 trades
Trade 1: IDM sweep → IOF/OB tap → M15 counter-trend maps → CHoCH on M15 → buy at hidden OB → 1:3 R:R
Hidden OB = last sell candle that swept previous liquidity + FVG above it
SL placement: below the safe low (low from which CHoCH originated)
Caution after major IDM close: market can still drop further
Trade 2: H4 OB sweep → early buyers trapped → liquidity swept → M15 CHoCH → buy at hidden OB → 1:6.9 R:R

OB sweep on HTF is NOT a problem — LTF structure alignment still produces high R:R entries
Entry confirmation: BOS + swing break on M15 = CHoCH confirmed → then trade new zone
Key zones on M15 after CHoCH: hidden order block (IOF) with FVG = highest priority entry
